msg: "{hit}" attributes the property of preventing, treating or curing a human disease. Art. 7(3) Reg (EU) 1169/2011 bans this for any food, in labelling and in advertising, and no authorisation can make it lawful. Delete the sentence.

"{hit}" is not an authorised wording. The Union Register (Reg (EU) 432/2012) authorises only "contributes to the normal function of the immune system", and only where the nutrient reaches 15 % of the NRV. Swap the wording and name the nutrient.
"{hit}" is a health claim with no entry in the Union Register, so Art. 10(1) Reg (EC) 1924/2006 forbids it. There is no authorised detox claim for any food or botanical. Remove it.

"{hit}" is a non-specific reference to general wellbeing. Art. 10(3) Reg (EC) 1924/2006 allows it only when a specific authorised health claim stands next to it, and this page carries none. Add the Register wording or cut the phrase.
"{hit}" states a rate or an amount of weight loss. Art. 12(b) Reg (EC) 1924/2006 prohibits that outright. Drop the figure and the timescale together.

"{hit}" refers to a recommendation by an individual health professional. Art. 12(c) Reg (EC) 1924/2006 prohibits it; only national associations covered by Art. 11 may be named. Remove the endorsement.

"{hit}" asserts proof of an effect on the body. Art. 6(1) Reg (EC) 1924/2006 requires every claim to rest on generally accepted scientific evidence, and Art. 10(1) permits only wordings already entered in the Union Register. Use the authorised wording or drop the phrase.

"{hit}" needs at least a 30 % reduction against a comparable product plus a statement of the characteristic that was reduced (Annex to Reg (EC) 1924/2006). No reduction of 30 % or more is stated on this page. Name the nutrient and the percentage.

"{hit}" may stand only where no mono- or disaccharide and no sweetening food was added, and where the food still contains sugars the Annex requires the added statement "CONTAINS NATURALLY OCCURRING SUGARS". That statement is missing.
